deadline: September 26 (Friday, 1:00 PM UK / 8:00 AM US Eastern — qualifying day, NOT Saturday)
central_unknown: Whether Ferrari will take Charles Leclerc's engine penalty at Baku remains unconfirmed after FP1/FP2. If he takes it, he becomes a massive overtake-points play starting from ~P18-P20; if not, his fantasy ceiling is significantly lower. Additionally, Lawson's return to Racing Bulls creates pricing algorithm uncertainty.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus #1 captain across all channels. ML projects 23.4 exp pts, ppm 2.07, LOW risk, DNF only 5%, pred P3→P3. Massive Monza score (93 pts) inflates projections but his floor is high. FanAmp labels him 1A. BoxBox ML ranks him #3 on expected but #1 on value (ppm 2.07) with lowest risk of all top drivers.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: ML's #1 recommended captain: exp 24.7 pts, proj 37.1 pts, ppm 1.1, MEDIUM risk, pred P1→P1. Topped FP1 and FP2 timing sheets. Betting lines moved him up to match Norris. FanAmp ranks him best #2 option if Leclerc doesn't take penalty. Channels favor Antonelli as captain but ML ranks Russell higher on raw expected points.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: FanAmp highlights Verstappen as top differential — P2 and P3 in FP1/FP2, betting odds moved ahead of Ferraris. However, ML is cautious: exp 15.2 pts, MEDIUM risk, DNF 0.17, pred P2→P6. Channels favor him but ML ranks him only #7 on expected points. High ceiling but notable downside risk.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: IF engine penalty is taken, becomes a 1B captain alongside Antonelli — massive overtake potential from P18-P20 on a street circuit with 2 DRS zones. FanAmp strongly advocates. Without penalty, still frees up budget vs. Russell/Norris. ML is bearish without penalty context: exp 12.1 pts, pred P5→P8. But penalty scenario could dramatically outperform ML baseline. Historical Baku specialist.

buy.name: Alex Albon
buy.note: Williams brought major chassis/weight-strip upgrade. Strong Baku history (2, 12, 13 pts last 3 years). Needs only 2 pts for price rise. In ~50% of global top 500. FanAmp and PolePosition both highlight as must-have. ML may underrate due to lack of upgrade data.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Audi brought massive 14-component upgrade package. Excellent budget replacement for $3M assets. Needs -3 pts for price rise (very achievable). BoxBox highlights as strong Pérez/Stroll replacement at 4.8M.

buy.name: Franco Colapinto
buy.note: Averaging 11.1 pts/race, outperforming teammate Gasly recently. Back-to-back 14 and 13 pt scores. Longest active non-DNF streak. PolePosition highlights as strong mid-budget option if you can't reach Lawson. Needs only 2 pts for minimum price rise.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Back at Racing Bulls after Hadjar's return. Scored 12, 2, 16 in his last 3 Red Bull races. Price dropped 0.6M — on sale. Major uncertainty around pricing algorithm: may need 27-35 pts for price rise depending on how F1 Fantasy handles inactive period. Strong driver but budget-building risk.

consider.name: Isack Hadjar
consider.note: Returned to Red Bull after wrist injury. ML projects 17.7 exp pts (value 1.22, #5 overall). Same pricing algorithm uncertainty as Lawson. Strong upside but unknown form after 3-race absence.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Benefits from Audi's 14-component upgrade. FanAmp says 'could be must-have.' Cheaper than Hulkenberg but less proven. Watch FP3 performance.

consider.name: Ollie Bearman
consider.note: BoxBox highlights at 5.8M — needs only 4 pts for min price rise, 9 for max. Had engine failure in FP2 though — must confirm car is repaired before selecting. Cheaper than Albon.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: Hit wall in FP2 but car looked repairable. Needs 7 pts for min price rise. FanAmp says viable if car is back on track. BoxBox ML not high on him but channels like the upside.

chips.name: Wildcard

chips.name: 3x Captain Boost
chips.reason: No explicit recommendation for Baku. BoxBox used 3x at Monza on Antonelli for huge returns. Save for a sprint weekend or a race where your captain pick has extreme confidence (lower CI range). Baku's street circuit variance makes this risky.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No channel recommended Limitless for Baku. BoxBox's Monza analysis showed 3x outperformed Limitless in certain setups. Save for a sprint weekend or when team prices are most imbalanced.

watch_items: Charles Leclerc engine penalty decision — likely confirmed after FP3 on Friday morning. This is the single biggest swing factor for team selection.
Ollie Bearman's engine repair status after FP2 failure — must be confirmed running in FP3 before selecting.
Arvid Lindblad car repair status after FP2 wall contact — same as Bearman, confirm before selection.
Kimi Antonelli hydraulics issue from FP1 — Mercedes got him back for FP2 but monitor FP3 for lingering problems.
Audi upgrade performance in FP3/qualifying — 14 components changed, could significantly boost Hulkenberg and Bortoleto.
Williams upgrade impact — new chassis designed to strip weight. Watch if Albon and Sainz can consistently exit Q1.
McLaren sidepod/aero upgrade effectiveness — Norris was P14 in FP1, need to see if this was staggered run plan or genuine struggle.
Liam Lawson and Isack Hadjar pricing algorithm — F1 Fantasy has not communicated how inactive periods affect 3-race rolling averages. Budget-building risk.
Friday qualifying deadline (not Saturday!) — lineups lock before qualifying at 1:00 PM UK time on Friday. Many managers will be at work.
arc: Baku kicks off a brutal stretch: three consecutive triple headers with only one-week breaks between them (Azerbaijan→Malaysia→Singapore, then USA→Mexico→Brazil, then Las Vegas→Qatar→Abu Dhabi). The key strategic arc is escaping $3M assets NOW while they're still avoidable — channels unanimously agree that Stroll, Pérez, and Cadillac drivers have been rank killers. Albon, Hulkenberg, and Colapinto are the budget bridges. The Audi and Williams upgrades debuting here will carry through the triple header, so their Baku performance sets expectations for Malaysia and Singapore. Lawson's return to Racing Bulls creates a potential value play over the next 2-3 races once his pricing normalizes. If Leclerc takes the penalty here, Ferrari may be fully healthy for Malaysia/Singapore — making this a short-term pain, long-term gain scenario. Save your power chips for sprint weekends or higher-confidence setups later in this marathon stretch.
